lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice placing inte after the verb in simple main clauses.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: Fika preferences and small corrections during a coffee break.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Saying what you do not want, do not do, or are not sure about.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik talk about coffee, tea, and work preferences, using polite negative statements without making the conversation heavy.

main_focus.name: main-clause negation with inte
main_focus.description: Put inte after the finite verb in simple statements and answers.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use negated main clauses naturally 4-5 times in the dialogue.

allowed_supporting_grammar: short answers with ja and nej

vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use fika vocabulary as the natural reason for saying no or correcting a small assumption.

dialogue_shape.opening: One speaker offers coffee or asks about a fika choice.
dialogue_shape.middle: They politely say what they do not drink or do not want today, with one or two alternatives.
dialogue_shape.ending: They settle on a simple fika choice and continue the break.

target_complexity.repetition: repeat inte in several main-clause positions without overloading the dialogue

focus: what one speaker does not want
what drink choice they choose instead
whether the negative statement is polite or corrective

sentence_focus: one negative sentence about working at home
